    15: - name: Set up complyctl NIST scanner on RHEL9

    17:   become: true
    18:   vars:
    19:     complyctl_bin: "{{ lookup('env', 'COMPLYCTL_BIN') | default('/tmp/complyctl', true) }}"
    20:     provider_bin: "{{ lookup('env', 'PROVIDER_BIN') | default(ansible_env.HOME + '/.complytime/providers/complyctl-provider-openscap', true) }}"
    21:     oras_version: "{{ lookup('env', 'ORAS_VERSION') | default('1.2.3', true) }}"
    22:     registry_port: "{{ lookup('env', 'REGISTRY_PORT')  | default('5500', true) }}"

    24:     # playbook_dir = .../utils/nist_sync/ansible
    25:     repo_root: "{{ playbook_dir | realpath + '/../../..' }}"

    29:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    30:     # complyctl binary
    31:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    32:     - name: Copy complyctl binary
    33:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    34:         src: "{{ complyctl_bin }}"
    35:         dest: /usr/local/bin/complyctl
    36:         mode: "0755"
    37: 
    38:     - name: Verify complyctl runs
    39:       ansible.builtin.command: /usr/local/bin/complyctl version
    40:       register: ver
    41:       changed_when: false
    42: 
    43:     - name: Show complyctl version
    44:       ansible.builtin.debug:
    45:         msg: "{{ ver.stdout }}"
    46: 
    47:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    48:     # complyctl-provider-openscap
    49:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    50:     - name: Create provider directory

    52:         path: /root/.local/share/complytime/providers

    60:         mode: "0755"
    61: 
    62:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    63:     # OCI registry — distribution/distribution binary (no podman required).
    64:     # Runs as a systemd service inside the VM listening on all interfaces.
    65:     # The host pushes bundles to ansible_host:{{ registry_port }} via oras;
    66:     # complyctl on the VM uses http://localhost:{{ registry_port }}.
    67:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    68:     - name: Check if registry binary is already installed
    69:       ansible.builtin.stat:
    70:         path: /usr/local/bin/registry
    71:       register: registry_bin_stat
    72: 
    73:     - name: Download distribution/distribution registry binary
    74:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
    75:         curl -sL \
    76:           "https://github.com/distribution/distribution/releases/download/v2.8.3/registry_2.8.3_linux_amd64.tar.gz" \
    77:           | tar -xz -C /usr/local/bin registry
    78:         chmod +x /usr/local/bin/registry

    80: 
    81:     - name: Create registry storage directory
    82:       ansible.builtin.file:
    83:         path: /var/lib/gemara-registry
    84:         state: directory
    85:         mode: "0755"
    86: 
    87:     - name: Write registry config
    88:       ansible.builtin.copy:
    89:         dest: /etc/gemara-registry.yml
    90:         mode: "0644"
    91:         content: |
    92:           version: 0.1
    93:           log:
    94:             level: warn
    95:           storage:
    96:             filesystem:
    97:               rootdirectory: /var/lib/gemara-registry
    98:             delete:
    99:               enabled: true
   100:           http:
   101:             addr: :{{ registry_port }}
   102: 
   103:     - name: Create systemd service for registry
   104:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   105:         dest: /etc/systemd/system/gemara-registry.service
   106:         mode: "0644"
   107:         content: |
   108:           [Unit]
   109:           Description=Gemara OCI Registry
   110:           After=network.target
   111:           [Service]
   112:           ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/registry serve /etc/gemara-registry.yml
   113:           Restart=always
   114:           RestartSec=3
   115:           [Install]
   116:           WantedBy=multi-user.target
   117: 
   118:     - name: Enable and start registry service
   119:       ansible.builtin.systemd_service:
   120:         name: gemara-registry
   121:         state: started
   122:         enabled: true
   123:         daemon_reload: true
   124: 
   125:     - name: Wait for registry to become ready
   126:       ansible.builtin.uri:
   127:         url: "http://localhost:{{ registry_port }}/v2/"
   128:         status_code: 200
   129:       retries: 15
   130:       delay: 2
   131:       register: registry_ready
   132:       until: registry_ready.status == 200
   133: 
   134:     - name: Registry is ready
   135:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   136:         msg: "OCI registry running at localhost:{{ registry_port }} (and {{ ansible_host }}:{{ registry_port }} from the host)"
   137: 
   138:     - name: Open registry port in the VM firewall
   139:       ansible.builtin.shell: |
   140:         firewall-cmd --add-port={{ registry_port }}/tcp --permanent
   141:         firewall-cmd --reload
   142:       args:
   143:         executable: /bin/bash
   144:       changed_when: true
   145:

   147:     # SCAP data stream — always copy the repo-built version.
   148:     # The system RPM (scap-security-guide) predates the nist_800_53 profile
   149:     # commit and will not contain that profile.  The built data stream must
   150:     # be deployed even if the RPM is already installed.
   151:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

   153:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   154:         src: "{{ repo_root }}/build/ssg-rhel9-ds.xml"
   155:         dest: "{{ ds_dest }}"
   156:         mode: "0644"
   157:         force: true
   158: 
   159:     - name: Confirm data stream has nist_800_53 profile
   160:       ansible.builtin.command: "grep -c nist_800_53 {{ ds_dest }}"
   161:       register: profile_check
   162:       changed_when: false
   163:       failed_when: profile_check.rc != 0 or profile_check.stdout | int == 0
   164: 
   165:     - name: Show data stream status
   166:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   167:         msg: "Data stream: {{ ds_dest }} — nist_800_53 profile present ({{ profile_check.stdout }} occurrences)"
   168:

   170:     # Summary
   171:     # -------------------------------------------------------------------------

   173:       ansible.builtin.debug:
   174:         msg: |

    34:     # does NOT run on a tagged deploy — and a key rotation is exactly a tagged deploy
    35:     # (make deploy TAGS=litellm,api,interpret,ntfy-alerts). Two gaps compound there:

    52: 
    53:             python3 -c "import secrets; print('sk-' + secrets.token_urlsafe(32))"
    54:             ansible-vault edit ansible/vars/secrets.yml
    55:       tags: [always]
    56: 
    57:     # --- Deploy provenance (#151) ------------------------------------------
    58:     #
    59:     # Tagged `always` for exactly the reason the assert above is: a TAGGED deploy is
    60:     # when drift happens, and pre_tasks are skipped unless tagged. `make deploy
    61:     # TAGS=pipeline` is the common case, so a provenance marker that only appeared on
    62:     # full deploys would be absent precisely when it is needed.
    63:     #

    72:     # strategy-dependent. The git reads are idempotent regardless.

    76:         chdir: "{{ playbook_dir }}/.."

    78:       changed_when: false
    79:       delegate_to: localhost
    80:       become: false
    81:       tags: [always]
    82: 
    83:     - name: Read the deploying checkout's branch

    86:         chdir: "{{ playbook_dir }}/.."

    88:       changed_when: false
    89:       delegate_to: localhost
    90:       become: false
    91:       tags: [always]

    93:     # Uncommitted changes mean the deployed bytes correspond to NO commit, so the SHA
    94:     # alone is a lie. Recorded rather than blocked: deploying a work-in-progress is a
    95:     # legitimate thing to do deliberately, and an unexplained hard failure here would
    96:     # just teach people to skip the check.
    97:     - name: Detect uncommitted changes in the deploying checkout
    98:       ansible.builtin.command:
    99:         cmd: git status --porcelain
   100:         chdir: "{{ playbook_dir }}/.."
   101:       register: _deploy_dirty
   102:       changed_when: false
   103:       delegate_to: localhost
   104:       become: false
   105:       tags: [always]
   106: 
   107:     - name: Look at the previous deploy's markers before overwriting them
   108:       ansible.builtin.stat:
   109:         path: "/opt/lamware/deploy-{{ item }}.json"

   112:       tags: [always]
   113: 
   114:     - name: Name the two previous markers
   115:       ansible.builtin.set_fact:
   116:         _prev_started: "{{ _prev_markers.results[0] }}"
   117:         _prev_completed: "{{ _prev_markers.results[1] }}"
   118:       tags: [always]
   119: 
   120:     - name: Ensure the provenance directory exists
   121:       ansible.builtin.file:
   122:         path: /opt/lamware
   123:         state: directory
   124:         mode: "0755"
   125:       tags: [always]
   126: 
   127:     # STARTED, not deployed. This runs before a single role, so it records what
   128:     # the deploy INTENDED. A play that aborts mid-way leaves this behind and
   129:     # nothing else — which is how a failed deploy on 2026-09-01 reported the
   130:     # full tag list while `grep -c single_shot_backend runner.py` returned 0 on
   131:     # the host (#515). The completed marker is written in post_tasks, where it
   132:     # can only exist if every role ran.
   133:     - name: Write the deploy STARTED marker
   134:       ansible.builtin.copy:
   135:         dest: /opt/lamware/deploy-started.json
   136:         mode: "0644"
   137:         content: |

   139:             {
   140:               "sha": _deploy_sha.stdout,
   141:               "branch": _deploy_branch.stdout,
   142:               "dirty": (_deploy_dirty.stdout | length) > 0,

   146:               "deployed_by": (lookup("env", "USER") | default("unknown", true)),

   148:           }}
   149:       tags: [always]
   150:

   153:         msg: >-

   155:           matching completed one, so the host is in whatever state that play
   156:           left it. Treat `make provenance` as unverified until this deploy ends.

   159:         - (not _prev_completed.stat.exists)

     2: - name: Hermes guest convergence - Hermes setup
     3:   # Hermes guest convergence - HERMES SETUP phase. Runs during the egress install
     4:   # window because the installer and tirith download need network access. Assumes
     5:   # setup-os.yml has mounted and owned the persistent Hermes state directory and
     6:   # prepared the service user's shell.
     7:   #
     8:   # Installs, all as the unprivileged `hermes` service user:
     9:   #   - the Hermes Agent (Nous installer) + its tirith pre-exec scanner,
    10:   #   - the OpenCode, Claude Code, and Codex coding-agent CLIs.
    11:   # Every install uses each vendor's official method (curl installer or GitHub
    12:   # release binary) — deliberately NOT npm: the guest egress firewall admits the
    13:   # vendors' installer/API/GitHub endpoints but not registry.npmjs.org.
    14:   #
    15:   # Run order: setup-os (egress open) -> setup-hermes (egress open) -> lock egress
    16:   # -> configure.
    17:   #
    18:   # Target only the host AAP passes via ansible_limit (e.g. hermes-hermes from the
    19:   # kubevirt dynamic inventory). `hosts: all` would run the installer across the
    20:   # whole fleet - match the linux_baseline convention instead.
    21:   hosts: "{{ ansible_limit | default('hermes-hermes') }}"
    22:   become: true
    23:   # Facts are gathered in pre_tasks after the connection is proven, so a
    24:   # freshly provisioned VM (whose sshd may not be up yet) doesn't fail at play
    25:   # start. For the live hermes VM the wait returns immediately.
    26:   gather_facts: false
    27:   vars:
    28:     hermes_user: hermes
    29:     hermes_home: /home/hermes
    30:     hermes_state_mount: "{{ hermes_home }}/.hermes"
    31:     hermes_install_url: "https://hermes-agent.nousresearch.com/install.sh"
    32:     # Non-sudo / service-user install: skip browser automation. A working browser
    33:     # needs system Chromium libs from `sudo npx playwright install-deps chromium`
    34:     # (a sudo/admin step that doesn't fit the non-sudo service-user model), so the
    35:     # installer would otherwise leave a non-functional Chromium in ~/.cache. Flip
    36:     # to false only after running that admin step out of band.
    37:     hermes_install_skip_browser: true
    38:     # NB: hermes_install_agent is NOT set here as a play var. Play vars outrank
    39:     # inventory group_vars, so defining it here would shadow a group_vars
    40:     # override (e.g. group_vars/hermes_test.yml sets it false for the broker-only
    41:     # test). It is referenced as `hermes_install_agent | default(true)` in the
    42:     # task conditions below, so it defaults to true (full agent) unless a
    43:     # group/host var sets it.
    44:     # Default broker minting policy (deny-not-clamp). Override with
    45:     # hermes_ghapp_policy. Scratch repos only until go-live widens it.
    46:     hermes_ghapp_policy_default:
    47:       allowed_repos:
    48:         - david-igou/hermes_github_app_plugin
    49:         - igou-io/igou-infrastructure
    50:       max_permissions:
    51:         contents: write
    52:         pull_requests: write
    53:         issues: write
    54:       default_permissions:
    55:         contents: read
    56:   pre_tasks:
    57:     - name: Wait for the VM's SSH to come up
    58:       ansible.builtin.wait_for_connection:
    59:         timeout: 300
    60: 
    61:     - name: Gather facts (after the connection is proven)

    63: 
    64:   tasks:
    65:     # When the full agent stack is skipped (broker-only test convergence), the
    66:     # linux_baseline step that normally creates the hermes service user isn't
    67:     # run, so ensure it here. For the live hermes flow (agent install on),
    68:     # setup-os already created the user and this is skipped.
    69:     - name: Ensure the hermes service user exists (broker-only convergence)
    70:       ansible.builtin.user:
    71:         name: "{{ hermes_user }}"
    72:         home: "{{ hermes_home }}"
    73:         shell: /bin/bash
    74:         create_home: true
    75:         state: present
    76:       become: true
    77:       when: not (hermes_install_agent | default(true) | bool)
    78: 
    79:     - name: Enable lingering for the hermes user (broker-only convergence)
    80:       ansible.builtin.command:
    81:         cmd: "loginctl enable-linger {{ hermes_user }}"
    82:       args:
    83:         creates: "/var/lib/systemd/linger/{{ hermes_user }}"
    84:       become: true
    85:       when: not (hermes_install_agent | default(true) | bool)
    86: 
    87:     - name: Own the Hermes state mount to the hermes user

    89:         path: "{{ hermes_state_mount }}"
    90:         state: directory
    91:         owner: "{{ hermes_user }}"
    92:         group: "{{ hermes_user }}"
    93:         recurse: true
    94:       become: true
